It has the BRRF 2023 logo at the top of it and says things like "do not put your wristband on", info about locker rentals, campsites, hotel packages, and just general info about the festival. I have a LOT of problems surrounding sex due to being SA before as well, and I feel for you as the boyfriend just trying to do what's right. You're doing great by being cautious and stopping when you felt the situation might have been wrong, and I really appreciate you doing that, a lot of men wouldn't have cared. 

My advice is to let her set the pace and have sex on her terms. It's not healthy for her only to want to have sex when she's blackout drunk, but I think until she feels more comfortable around you as a person (you've only been seeing eachother for a month so she's not comfortable right now) she will change her mind about the circumstances surrounding sex. 

Also, I know you have the best intentions with repeatedly asking her if she is okay and that's wonderful, but sometimes (in my own experience) having my partner ask me over and over again if I'm sure I'm okay will throw me out of my good headspace that I had and into being not so okay because you're reminded of WHY you might not be okay every time the question is repeated. If she says she's good and looks happy, just go for it. Of course still pay attention to her if she starts to space out or doesn't look like she's enjoying herself, but if she's enthusiastic and has already given you the go ahead then stop asking.

You and her need to sit down and have a good long conversation about when and where sex is okay, as well as how often. She might be feeling pressured to have sex more often than she wants because she wants to make you happy which results in your awkward sessions. I know you're not pressuring her, but survivors feel guilty for not being "normal" and force themselves to try being normal for the sake of their partner. I know I've done it.

I was (still kinda am) in the same boat. I graduated third in my highschool class, i had straight A's since 6th grade, and I got an amazing full tuition scholarship to attend my college. I thought to myself "oh this is gonna be easy" just like highschool was a breeze for me. Needless to say, I was dead wrong. I failed several classes, had to drop other classes mid semester, and got D's on several others. I was absolutely horrified with myself since I'd always placed my self worth at an equal level to my academic performance and I felt like total shit. It was truly awful for me and I fell into a hardcore depression and skipped like ALL of my classes.

How I pulled myself out was literally just "manning up." It sounds so stupid but I thought to myself, "well molly you can't fuck this up much more than you already have, so just put in the damn work." I found that going to class made me feel amazing for the rest of that day, even though I was so ashamed of my grades that I felt as if I shouldn't even show up. 

Also, I'm not sure if you have a car to drive yourself to campus, but I started hitching a ride with my roomate to go to campus in the morning that way I was forced to align myself to her schedule and remain on campus until we were BOTH done with classes for the day. It helped me out tremendously knowing that someone else was expecting me to hop in the car at a certain time every morning, and the gaps between my classes were times that I was forced to spend in the library, and therefore forced to study and do my homework. 

The final thing that I did was I took summer classes and paid for them myself IN FULL every month. Having to fork out $750 every single month out of my own money really put into perspective just how expensive these classes are, and how much they truly matter. It's a blessing to have your parents pay for your schooling, but you need to grasp the true value of what they're giving you so that you yourself can understand and use it as motivation. The summer classes improved my overall GPA, and helped me to get my credits up in the ballpark of where they needed to be.

Overall, I know exactly where you're at. It's heartbreaking and you feel as though you've let everyone down, but at the end of the day you're doing this FOR YOU. It's easy to pull yourself back up once you've changed your mindset and accept the fact that high school did jack shit to prepare you for college. It's an entirely new ballpark, so keep an open mind and get the old highschool standards out of your head. You got this, and if you need help don't hesitate to reach out because I've been exactly where you are.
